{{Blockquote|text=The third Umpire will officiate in regard to TV replays only when the Umpires on the field have referred a decision to him in regard to hit wicket, run out, caught or stumping appeals.}}{{Blockquote|text=Either the on field or third umpire shall be entitled to call for a TV replay to assist him in making a decision about whether the fieldsman had any part of his person in contact with the ball when he touched or crossed the boundary line or whether a four or six had been scored (refer to Regulation of ICC Full Members, Clause 2).}}[[Michael Atherton]], opening batsman for England, said after he was given out (caught) by the third umpire in the third Test in Adelaide in 1998: "In my opinion the third umpire should be restricted to line decisions [run outs, stumpings and boundaries]. What people are looking for from a third umpire is 100 per cent correct decision-making, but that's a Utopia that cannot exist. There's often doubt about non-line decisions made by the third umpire. There is no substitute at the end of the day for the player's word out in the middle and the two umpire's control of the decision making process."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atherton: cut powers of third umpire (13 December 1998) |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/atherton-cut-powers-of-third-umpire-13-december-1998-74736 |website=ESPNCricinfo}}</ref>

On 26 June 2000, Bangladesh were granted Test status, and played their first match on 1 November 2000.<ref>{{Cite news |last=staff |first=Cricket Unlimited |date=26 June 2000 |title=Bangladesh granted Test status |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2000/jun/26/cricket5 |access-date=17 May 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=ESPNcricinfo.com Statsguru - Bangladesh - Test matches - Team analysis |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/team/25.html?class=1;template=results;type=team;view=results |access-date=17 May 2026 |website=Cricinfo}}</ref>

== Twenty-first century ==

=== Expansion of neutral umpires and relocation of the ICC ===
After the trial of one neutral umpire per Test in 1992, two neutrals were made mandatory in 2002, beginning with India’s tour of the West Indies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rajesh |first=S |date=16 April 2011 |title=Neutral umpires |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/cricket-s-turning-points-neutral-umpires-511175 |access-date=17 May 2026 |website=ESPNCricinfo}}</ref>

In 2005, after months of speculation, the ICC relocated from Lord’s to Dubai. Tax advantages were cited as one of the reasons for the move.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Averis |first=Mike |date=1 July 2004 |title=ICC may turn its back on Lord's |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2004/jul/01/cricket |access-date=17 May 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Long |first=Jon |date=28 July 2005 |title=ICC to relocate to Dubai on 1 August 2005 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/icc-to-relocate-to-dubai-on-1-august-2005-214500 |access-date=17 May 2026 |website=ESPNCricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=8 March 2005 |title=ICC moves to Dubai |url=https://www.espn.com.au/cricket/story/_/id/23113856/icc-moves-dubai |access-date=17 May 2026 |website=www.espn.com.au}}</ref>

=== Introduction of the Decision Review System ===
{{Main|Decision Review System}}
A Player Referral system was first tested in an India v. Sri Lanka match in 2008,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/news/53230-umpiring-decision-review-system-on-the-cards|title=Umpiring decision review system on the cards – NDTV Sports|last=NDTVSports.com|access-date=29 November 2016|archive-date=25 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160825204051/http://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/news/53230-umpiring-decision-review-system-on-the-cards|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/umpire-review-system-to-be-trialled-in-sri-lanka-india-tests-354984|title=Umpire review system to be trialled in Sri Lanka-India Tests|website=ESPN Cricinfo|date=16 June 2008}}</ref> and was officially launched by the ICC on 24 November 2009, during the first Test between [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] and [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]] at the [[University Oval, Dunedin|University Oval]] in [[Dunedin]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cricketnext.in.com/news/decision-review-system-set-for-debut/45336-13.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091126234422/http://cricketnext.in.com/news/decision-review-system-set-for-debut/45336-13.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 November 2009|title=Decision Review System set for debut|date=23 November 2009|publisher=Cricketnext.in|access-date=18 February 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cricinfo.com/ci-icc/content/story/436290.html|title=Official debut for enhanced review system|date=23 November 2009|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=18 February 2010|archive-date=10 January 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100110054708/http://www.cricinfo.com/ci-icc/content/story/436290.html|url-status=live}}</ref> It later became known as the Decision Review System.

=== Introduction of day/night Tests ===
{{Main|Day/night cricket}}
Amid growing concern over dwindling viewership in the late 2000s,<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Silgardo |first=Dustin |date=20 November 2019 |title=A brief history of pink-ball cricket |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/a-brief-history-of-pink-ball-cricket-1207107 |access-date=21 October 2025 |website=ESPNCricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=30 June 2014 |title=Day-night Tests one step closer |url=https://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/day-night-tests-one-step-closer/040b7g4r9 |access-date=20 October 2025 |website=SBS News |language=en}}</ref> numerous trials were held in the early 2010s which culminated in day/night Tests being permitted by the ICC in 2012, and the first day/night match was between [[New Zealand cricket team in Australia in 2015–16|Australia and New Zealand]] at the [[Adelaide Oval]] in November 2015. These matches start later in the day and continue into the evening, necessitating the use of a pink ball to aid in visibility.<ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Red, White & Pink Cricket Balls: What is the Difference? |url=https://westernsportscentre.com.au/pages/red-white-pink-cricket-balls-what-is-the-difference |access-date=20 October 2025 |website=Western Sports Centre |language=en}}</ref>

=== Admission of Afghanistan and Ireland ===
On 22 June 2017, Afghanistan and Ireland were granted Test status.<ref>{{Cite web |last=icc |date=22 June 2017 |title=Ireland and Afghanistan ICC newest full members amid wide-ranging governance reform |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/ireland-and-afghanistan-icc-newest-full-members-amid-wide-ranging-governance-reform |access-date=17 May 2026 |website=icc |language=en}}</ref> Ireland played their first Test on 11 May 2018,<ref>{{Cite web |title=ESPNcricinfo.com Statsguru – Ireland – Test matches – Team analysis |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/team/29.html?class=1;template=results;type=team;view=results |access-date=17 May 2026 |website=Cricinfo}}</ref> while Afghanistan played their first Test 14 June 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ESPNcricinfo.com Statsguru – Afghanistan – Test matches – Team analysis |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/team/40.html?class=1;template=results;type=team;view=results |access-date=17 May 2026 |website=Cricinfo}}</ref>

=== Introduction of the World Test Championship ===
{{Main|World Test Championship}}
After years of delays and cancelled tournaments, the World Test Championship was inaugurated in 2019 to offer a competition for the highest level of the game. Nine of the twelve Test playing nations participated, with [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] winning the final by 8 wickets over India.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IND vs NZ Cricket Scorecard, Final at Southampton, June 18 – 23, 2021 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-world-test-championship-2019-2021-1195334/india-vs-new-zealand-final-1249875/full-scorecard |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251209162946/https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-world-test-championship-2019-2021-1195334/india-vs-new-zealand-final-1249875/full-scorecard |archive-date=9 December 2025 |access-date=17 May 2026 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Test status==
Test matches are the highest level of cricket, played between national representative teams with "Test status", as determined by the [[International Cricket Council]]. {{As of|June 2017}}, twelve national teams have Test status, the most recently promoted being Afghanistan and Ireland on 22 June 2017.<ref name=AI_test>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/40364481 |title=Ireland & Afghanistan awarded Test status by International Cricket Council |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=22 June 2017 |website=BBC News |access-date=22 June 2017 |archive-date=22 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170622143835/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/40364481 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Teams with Test status===
Test status is conferred upon a country or group of countries by the ICC. There are currently twelve men's teams that have been granted this status: international teams that do not have Test status can play [[first-class cricket]] in the [[ICC Intercontinental Cup]], under conditions which are similar to Tests.

The teams with Test status (with the date of each team's Test debut) are:
#{{cr|Australia}} ([[English cricket team in Australia and New Zealand in 1876–77#First Test|15 March 1877]])
#{{cr|England}} ([[English cricket team in Australia and New Zealand in 1876–77#First Test|15 March 1877]])
#{{cr|South Africa}} ([[English cricket team in South Africa in 1888–89#First Test|12 March 1889]])
#{{cr|West Indies}} ([[West Indian cricket team in England in 1928#First Test, Lord's, 23-26 June 1928|23 June 1928]])
#{{cr|New Zealand}} ([[English cricket team in New Zealand in 1929–30#First Test|10 January 1930]])
#{{cr|India}} ([[Indian cricket team in England in 1932#Test summary|25 June 1932]])
#{{cr|Pakistan}} ([[Pakistani cricket team in India in 1952–53#1st Test|16 October 1952]])
#{{cr|Sri Lanka}} ([[English cricket team in Sri Lanka in 1981–82#Only Test|17 February 1982]])
#{{cr|Zimbabwe}} ([[Indian cricket team in Zimbabwe in 1992–93#Only Test|18 October 1992]])
#{{cr|Bangladesh}} ([[Indian cricket team in Bangladesh in 2000–01#Only Test|10 November 2000]])
#{{cr|Ireland}} ([[Pakistani cricket team in Ireland in 2018#Only Test|11 May 2018]])
#{{cr|Afghanistan|2013}} ([[Afghan cricket team in India in 2018#Only Test|14 June 2018]])

Nine of these teams represent independent sovereign nations: the [[England cricket team]] represents the [[countries of the United Kingdom|constituent countries]] of [[England]] and [[Wales]], the West Indies is a combined team from fifteen Caribbean nations and territories, and Ireland represents both the [[Republic of Ireland]] and [[Northern Ireland]].

Following the [[D'Oliveira affair]] in 1969, [[History of cricket in South Africa from 1970–71 to 1990|South Africa]] was suspended from all forms of cricket from 1970 until the end of the [[Apartheid|apartheid regime]] in [[Negotiations to end apartheid in South Africa|1991]].

Zimbabwe's Test status was voluntarily suspended in 2006 because of very poor performances, but its Test status was reinstated in August 2011.<ref>[http://www.voanews.com/zimbabwe/news/Zimbabwe-Cricket-Resume-Test-Play-After-Six-Year-Break-126790218.html Zimbabwe Cricket Side Resume International Test Play After Six-Year Break] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120131101339/http://www.voanews.com/zimbabwe/news/Zimbabwe-Cricket-Resume-Test-Play-After-Six-Year-Break-126790218.html |date=31 January 2012 }} – [[Voice of America]].</ref>

===Statistics===
{{main|List of Test cricket records}}
For [[cricket statistics|statistical purposes]], Tests are considered to be a subset of [[first-class cricket]]. Performances in first-class matches count towards only the first-class statistical record, but performances in Test matches count towards both the Test statistics and the first-class statistics.

Statisticians have developed criteria to determine which matches count as Tests if they were played before the formal definition of Test status. There have been exceptional circumstances including the simultaneous England touring sides of 1891–92 ([[English cricket team in Australia in 1891–92|in Australia]] and [[English cricket team in South Africa in 1891–92|South Africa]]) and 1929–30 ([[English cricket team in the West Indies in 1929–30|in the West Indies]] and [[English cricket team in New Zealand in 1929–30|New Zealand]]), all of whose international matches are deemed to have Test status.

In 1970, a series of five "Test matches" was played in England between England and a Rest of the World XI: these matches, originally scheduled between England and South Africa, were amended after South Africa was suspended from international cricket due to their government's [[apartheid]] policies. Although initially given Test status and included as Test matches in some record books, including ''[[Wisden Cricketers' Almanack]]'', this was later withdrawn, and a principle was established that official Test matches can only be between nations (the geographically and demographically small countries of the West Indies have, since 1928, fielded a coalition side).

Despite this principle, in 2005, the ICC ruled that the six-day [[2005 ICC Super Series|Super Series]] match that took place that October between Australia and a World XI was an official Test match: some cricket writers and statisticians, including [[Bill Frindall]], have ignored the ICC's ruling and exclude this match from their records.

The series of "Test matches" played in Australia between Australia and a World XI in 1971–72, and the commercial "[[World Series Cricket|Supertests]]" organised by [[Kerry Packer]] as part of his [[World Series Cricket]] enterprise played between "WSC Australia", "WSC World XI" and "WSC West Indies" from 1977 to 1979, have never been regarded as official Test matches as of 2021.

==Conduct of the game==
===Playing time===
{{See also|Playing time (cricket)}}
A standard day of Test cricket consists of three sessions of two hours each, the break between sessions being 40 minutes for lunch and 20 minutes for tea. However, the times of sessions and intervals may be altered in certain circumstances: if bad weather or a change of innings occurs close to a scheduled break, the break may be taken immediately; if there has been a loss of playing time, for example because of bad weather, the session times may be adjusted to make up the lost time; if the batting side is nine [[dismissal (cricket)|wickets]] down at the scheduled tea break, then the interval may be delayed until either 30 minutes has elapsed or the team is ''all out'';<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lords.org/laws-and-spirit/laws-of-cricket/laws/law-15-intervals,41,AR.html |title=The Laws of Cricket – Law 15.8 |publisher=Lords.org |access-date=18 July 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121124062128/http://www.lords.org/laws-and-spirit/laws-of-cricket/laws/law-15-intervals,41,AR.html |archive-date=24 November 2012}}</ref> the final session may be extended by up to 30 minutes if 90 or more [[over (cricket)|overs]] have not been [[bowling (cricket)|bowled]] in that day's play (subject to any reduction for adverse weather);<ref>{{cite web |url=http://l.yimg.com/t/icccricket/pdfs/test_playing_conditions.pdf |title=ICC Standard Test match Playing Conditions ('Playing Conditions') cl 16.1.1 |access-date=18 July 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111201928/http://l.yimg.com/t/icccricket/pdfs/test_playing_conditions.pdf |archive-date=11 January 2012}}</ref> the final session may be extended by 30 minutes (except on the 5th day) if the umpires believe the result can be decided within that time.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://l.yimg.com/t/icccricket/pdfs/test_playing_conditions.pdf |title=Playing Conditions cl 16.2 |access-date=18 July 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111201928/http://l.yimg.com/t/icccricket/pdfs/test_playing_conditions.pdf |archive-date=11 January 2012}}</ref>

Today, Test matches are scheduled to be played across five consecutive days. However, in the [[History of Test cricket from 1877 to 1883|early days]] of Test cricket, matches were played for three or four days. [[Irish cricket team in England in 2023#Only Test|England hosted Ireland at Lord's]] on 1 June 2023 for a four-day test.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ireland tour of England |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ireland-in-england-2023-1336035/england-vs-ireland-only-test-1336127/live-cricket-score |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=1 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230531013332/https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ireland-in-england-2023-1336035/england-vs-ireland-only-test-1336127/live-cricket-score |archive-date=31 May 2023 |language=en |date=1 June 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> There were also frequent six-day tests until the 1970s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Test matches {{!}} Team records {{!}} Longest matches (by days) |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/longest-matches-by-days-284023 |access-date=29 December 2024 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en |archive-date=30 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241230000100/https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/longest-matches-by-days-284023 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Four-day Test matches were last played in 1973, between [[Pakistani cricket team in New Zealand in 1972–73|New Zealand and Pakistan]].<ref name="NZPak">{{cite web |title=Cremer senses opportunity in shorter contest |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/cremer-senses-opportunity-in-shorter-contest-1130012 |access-date=19 December 2017 |website=ESPNcricinfo |archive-date=29 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220529081602/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/cremer-senses-opportunity-in-shorter-contest-1130012 |url-status=live}}</ref> Until the 1980s, it was usual to include a 'rest day', often a Sunday. There have also been '[[Timeless Test]]s', which have no predetermined maximum time. In 2005, Australia played a match scheduled for six days against a World XI, which the ICC sanctioned as an official Test match, though the match reached a conclusion on the fourth day. In October 2017, the ICC approved a request for a four-day Test match, between [[Zimbabwean cricket team in South Africa in 2017–18#Only Test|South Africa and Zimbabwe]], which started on 26 December 2017 and ended on the second day, 27 December.<ref name="approve">{{cite web |title=Test, ODI leagues approved by ICC Board |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/test-odi-leagues-approved-by-icc-board-1123784 |access-date=13 October 2017 |website=ESPNcricinfo |date=13 October 2017 |archive-date=16 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210516004434/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/test-odi-leagues-approved-by-icc-board-1123784 |url-status=live}}</ref> The ICC trialled the four-day Test format until the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]].<ref name="trial">{{cite web |title=South Africa to play Zimbabwe in inaugural four-day Test |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/south-africa-to-play-zimbabwe-in-inaugural-four-day-test-1123807 |access-date=13 October 2017 |website=ESPNcricinfo |date=13 October 2017 |archive-date=13 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413074910/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/south-africa-to-play-zimbabwe-in-inaugural-four-day-test-1123807 |url-status=live}}</ref> In December 2019, [[Cricket Australia]] were considering playing four-day Tests, subject to consensus with other Test nations.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/cricket/australian-cricket-board-to-seriously-consider-four-day-test-matches-1.957158 |title=Australian cricket board to 'seriously consider' four-day Test matches |work=The National |date=28 December 2019 |access-date=28 December 2019 |archive-date=28 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191228172132/https://www.thenational.ae/sport/cricket/australian-cricket-board-to-seriously-consider-four-day-test-matches-1.957158 |url-status=live}}</ref> Later the same month, the ICC considered the possibility of making four-day Test matches mandatory for the [[World Test Championship|ICC World Test Championship]] from 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=ICC to consider mandatory four-day Tests |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/icc-to-consider-mandatory-four-day-tests-1211511 |access-date=30 December 2019 |website=ESPNcricinfo |archive-date=25 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125124640/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/icc-to-consider-mandatory-four-day-tests-1211511 |url-status=live}}</ref>

There have been attempts by the ICC, the sport's governing body, to introduce [[Day/night Test|day-night Test matches]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lord's could host first day night Test in May 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/lord-s-could-host-first-day-night-test-in-may-2010-397240 |access-date=18 July 2013 |website=ESPNcricinfo |archive-date=22 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422020105/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/lord-s-could-host-first-day-night-test-in-may-2010-397240 |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2012, the International Cricket Council passed playing conditions that allowed for the staging of day-night Test matches.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.wisdenindia.com/cricket-news/icc-paves-day-night-tests/32709 |title=ICC paves way for Day-Night Tests |website=Wisden India |date=29 October 2012 |access-date=30 October 2012 |archive-date=30 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630231143/http://www.wisdenindia.com/cricket-news/icc-paves-day-night-tests/32709 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The first day-night Test took place during [[New Zealand cricket team in Australia in 2015–16|New Zealand's tour to Australia]] in November 2015.<ref name="Adelaide">{{cite web |title=First day-night Test for Adelaide Oval |date=29 June 2015 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/first-day-night-test-for-adelaide-oval-892403 |access-date=29 June 2015 |website=ESPNcricinfo |archive-date=8 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210508194706/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/first-day-night-test-for-adelaide-oval-892403 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Play===
{{further|Cricket#Laws and gameplay}}
Test cricket is played in ''innings'' (the word denotes both the singular and the plural). In each innings, one team [[batting (cricket)|bats]] and the other [[bowling (cricket)|bowls]] (or [[fielding (cricket)|fields]]). Ordinarily four innings are played in a Test match, and each team bats twice and bowls twice. Before the start of play on the first day, the two team captains and the match referee [[toss (cricket)|toss a coin]]; the captain who wins the toss decides whether his team will bat or bowl first.

In the following scenarios, the team that bats first is referred to as ''Team A'' and their opponents as ''Team B''.

Usually the teams will alternate at the completion of each innings. Thus, Team A will bat (and Team B will bowl) until its innings ends, and then Team B will bat and Team A will bowl. When Team B's innings ends, Team A begin their second innings, and this is followed by Team B's second innings. The winning team is the one that scores more runs in their two innings.

A team's innings ends in one of the following ways:<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lords.org/mcc/laws-of-cricket/laws/law-13-innings/ |title=Law 13 – Innings |work=The Laws of Cricket |publisher=Marylebone Cricket Club |access-date=22 December 2017 |archive-date=1 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001123108/https://www.lords.org/mcc/laws-of-cricket/laws/law-13-innings/ |url-status=live}}</ref>
* The team is "all out". This typically occurs when a team has lost ten wickets (ten of the eleven batters having been [[Dismissal (cricket)|dismissed]], so that they can no longer present a pair of batters) and are "bowled out" (regardless of how they were out). It may occasionally occur with the loss of fewer wickets if one or more batters are unavailable to bat (through injury, for example).
* The team's captain [[Declaration and forfeiture|declares]] the innings closed, usually because they believe they have enough runs. A declaration before the innings starts is called an innings forfeiture.
* The prescribed number of overs has been bowled.
* The prescribed time for the match expires.

Although not listed in Law 13.3, the fourth innings will effectively also end when the match ends due to the team scoring the required number of runs to win.

If, at the completion of Team B's first innings, Team A leads by at least 200 runs, the captain of Team A may (but is not required to) order Team B to have ''their'' second innings next. This is called enforcing the [[follow-on]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lords.org/mcc/laws-of-cricket/laws/law-14-the-follow-on/ |title=Law 14 – The follow-on |work=The Laws of Cricket |publisher=Marylebone Cricket Club |access-date=29 September 2017 |archive-date=22 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622060157/https://www.lords.org/mcc/laws-of-cricket/laws/law-14-the-follow-on/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In this case, the usual order of the third and fourth innings is reversed: Team A will bat in the fourth innings. The purpose of this is to give Team A the opportunity to bowl Team B out for fewer runs than Team A's lead and thus [[win by an innings]], which has been achieved in 197 out of 348 Tests (56.6%) in which the follow-on has been enforced. It is rare for a team forced to follow on to win the match; in Test cricket this has only happened four times.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 June 2025 |title=Test Cricket – Match Records and Statistics – Miscellaneous |url=https://howstat.com/cricket/statistics/Matches/MatchFollowOn.asp |access-date=17 June 2025 |website=HowSTAT |archive-date=13 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250913025427/https://howstat.com/cricket/statistics/Matches/MatchFollowOn.asp |url-status=live }}</ref> Australia was the losing team on three occasions, losing twice to England, in 1894 and in 1981, and once to India in 2001.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Australia has lost 3 Times by Enforcing Follow-On |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/australia-loses-after-follow-on |access-date=6 June 2024 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en |archive-date=27 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240527053823/https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/australia-loses-after-follow-on |url-status=live }}</ref> Most recently, on 24 February 2023, England lost to New Zealand by one run after enforcing the follow-on.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://howstat.com/cricket/Statistics/Matches/MatchFollowOn.asp?FollowOn=T&Result=Lost |title=Matches where Follow-On Available {{!}} Lost by Side Enforcing Follow-On |website=HowSTAT |access-date=3 March 2023 |archive-date=4 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404233752/http://howstat.com/cricket/Statistics/Matches/MatchFollowOn.asp?FollowOn=T&Result=Lost |url-status=live }}</ref>

If the whole of the first day's play of a Test match has been lost because of bad weather or other reasons like bad light, then Team A may enforce the follow-on if Team B's first innings total is 150 or more fewer than Team A's. During the [[New Zealand cricket team in England in 2013#2nd Test|2nd Test]] between England and New Zealand at [[Headingley Cricket Ground|Headingley]] in 2013, England batted first after the first day was lost because of rain.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/current/match/566922.html |title=2nd Test: England v New Zealand at Leeds, May 24–28, 2013 &#124; Cricket Scorecard |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 July 2013 |archive-date=24 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130624090021/http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/current/match/566922.html |url-status=live}}</ref> New Zealand, batting second, scored 180 runs fewer than England, meaning England could have enforced the follow-on, though they chose not to. This is similar to four-day first-class cricket, where the follow-on can be enforced if the difference is 150 runs or more. If the Test is two days or fewer then the follow-on value is 100 runs.

After 80 overs, the captain of the bowling side may take a [[Cricket ball|new ball]], although this is not required.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lords.org/mcc/laws-of-cricket/laws/law-4-the-ball/ |title=Law 4 – The ball |work=The Laws of Cricket |publisher=Marylebone Cricket Club |access-date=29 September 2017 |archive-date=1 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001123047/https://www.lords.org/mcc/laws-of-cricket/laws/law-4-the-ball/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The captain will usually take the new ball: being harder and smoother than an old ball, a new ball generally favours faster bowlers who can make it bounce more variably. The roughened, softer surface of an old ball can be more conducive to spin bowlers, or those using [[swing bowling#Reverse swing|reverse swing]]. The captain may delay the decision to take the new ball if he wishes to continue with his spinners (because the pitch favours spin). After a new ball has been taken, should an innings last a further 80 overs, then the captain will have the option to take another new ball.

A Test match will produce a [[Result (cricket)|result]] by means of one of six scenarios:

*'''All four innings are complete.''' The team batting fourth are ''all out'' before overtaking the other team, usually before matching the other team's score. The team that batted third are the winners by a margin equal to the difference in the aggregate runs scored by the two teams (for example, "Team A won by 95 runs"). Very rarely (in over 2,000 Test matches played, [[Tied Test|it has only happened twice]]) the scores can end level, resulting in a [[Result (cricket)#Tie|tie]].
*'''The team batting in the fourth innings overtakes the opposing team's run total.''' The match ends, and the team batting fourth is the winner by a margin equal to the number of wickets still to fall in the innings (for example, "Team B won by five wickets").
*'''The third innings concludes with the team that batted twice still trailing the team that batted once.''' The match ends without playing a fourth innings. The team that batted only once is the winner by a margin equal to "an innings" plus the difference in aggregate run totals of the teams (for example, "Team A won by an innings and 26 runs").
*'''Time for the match expires without a result being reached.''' This usually occurs at the end of the last day of the match. The result is a [[Result (cricket)#Draw|draw]]: there is no winner, no matter how superior the position of one of the sides. Rain causing a loss of playing time is a common factor in drawn matches, although matches may be drawn even without interference from the weather: usually as a result of poor time management or an intentional effort on the part of one team to avoid losing.
*'''The match is abandoned because the ground is declared unfit for play.''' This has occurred three times, resulting each time in a draw being declared: England v Australia at [[Headingley Cricket Ground|Headingley]], [[Leeds]], 1975 (vandalism);<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/august/19/newsid_2534000/2534763.stm |work=BBC News |title=On This Day: 19 August |access-date=18 December 2010 |archive-date=7 March 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080307132506/http://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/august/19/newsid_2534000/2534763.stm |url-status=live}}</ref> West Indies v England at [[Sabina Park]], [[Kingston, Jamaica]], 1998 (dangerous ground);<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/current/match/63783.html |title=1st Test: West Indies v England at Kingston, Jan 29 – Feb 2, 1998 &#124; Cricket Scorecard |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 July 2013 |archive-date=30 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130830204624/http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/current/match/63783.html |url-status=live}}</ref> West Indies v England at [[Sir Vivian Richards Stadium]], [[Antigua]], 2009 (dangerous ground).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/wiveng2009/engine/current/match/352662.html |title=2nd Test: West Indies v England at North Sound, Feb 13–17, 2009 &#124; Cricket Scorecard |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 July 2013 |archive-date=17 September 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130917101734/http://www.espncricinfo.com/wiveng2009/engine/current/match/352662.html |url-status=live}}</ref>
*'''The match is awarded through a forfeiture.''' If a team refuses to take the field of play, the umpires may award the match to the opposing team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lords.org/mcc/laws-of-cricket/laws/law-16-the-result/ |title=Law 16 – The result |work=The Laws of Cricket |publisher=Marylebone Cricket Club |access-date=29 June 2017 |archive-date=1 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001123036/https://www.lords.org/mcc/laws-of-cricket/laws/law-16-the-result/ |url-status=live}}</ref> This has only happened once in Test cricket, in the [[2006 ball-tampering controversy|2006 fourth Test between England and Pakistan]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2009/feb/01/england-pakistan-oval |work=The Guardian |location=London |title=England awarded abandoned Oval Test 'win' |date=1 February 2009 |access-date=27 March 2010 |archive-date=28 February 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228152222/http://www.theguardian.com/sport/2009/feb/01/england-pakistan-oval |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/cricket/england/5268560.stm |work=BBC News |title=Test abandoned after ball dispute |date=20 August 2006 |access-date=27 March 2010 |archive-date=21 March 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080321201943/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/cricket/england/5268560.stm |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Clothing and equipment===
{{main|Cricket clothing and equipment}}
[[File:Pollock to Hussey.jpg|thumb|right|Test cricketers playing in their whites]]
Traditionally cricketers play in all-white kit. Unlike in [[limited overs cricket]], this remains the case in Test cricket, as mandated by the ICC Clothing and Equipment Regulations.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://images.icc-cricket.com/image/upload/prd/vou5znt1fvbkl0ucvqll.pdf |title=Clothing and equipment rules and regulations |publisher=[[International Cricket Council]] |access-date=3 March 2024 |archive-date=3 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240303232044/https://images.icc-cricket.com/image/upload/prd/vou5znt1fvbkl0ucvqll.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Competitions==
===Tours===
{{main|Category:International cricket tours}}
Test cricket is almost always played as a series of matches between two countries, with all matches in the series taking place in the same country (the host). Often there is a perpetual trophy that is awarded to the winner, the most famous of which is [[the Ashes]] contested between England and Australia. There have been two exceptions to the bilateral nature of Test cricket: the [[1912 Triangular Tournament]], a three-way competition between England, Australia and South Africa (hosted by England), and the [[Asian Test Championship]], an event held in 1998–99 and 2001–02.

The number of matches in Test series has varied from one to seven.<ref name="Seven tests">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/current/match/63065.html |title=Australia v England, Seventh Test, 1970–71 |work=Cricinfo |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 July 2013 |archive-date=20 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170620143752/http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/current/match/63065.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Up until the early 1990s,<ref name="Neutral umpires">{{cite web |last=Rajesh |first=S. |date=16 April 2011 |title=Neutral umpires |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/cricket-s-turning-points-neutral-umpires-511175 |access-date=30 March 2012 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |archive-date=27 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201227020752/http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/cricket-s-turning-points-neutral-umpires-511175 |url-status=live}}</ref> Test series between international teams were organised between the two national cricket organisations with [[Umpire (cricket)|umpires]] provided by the home team. With the entry of more countries into Test cricket, and a wish by the ICC to maintain public interest in Tests in the face of the popularity of [[One Day International|One Day International cricket]], a rotation system was introduced that sees all ten Test teams playing each other over a six-year cycle, and an official [[ICC Men's Test Team Rankings|ranking system]] (with a trophy held by the highest-ranked team). In this system, umpires are provided by the ICC. An [[Elite Panel of ICC Umpires|elite panel of umpires]] was maintained since 2002, and the panel is supplemented by an additional [[International Panel of ICC Umpires|International Panel]] that includes three umpires named by each Test-playing country. The elite umpires officiate almost all Test matches, though usually not Tests involving their home country.

===World Test Championship===
{{main|World Test Championship}}
After years of delays since proposals began in 2009, a league competition for Test cricket was held in [[2019–2021 World Test Championship|2019–2021]]. Arranged as a bilateral series in various countries with one team as host and another team as visitor. The length of each series varies between 2 and 5 matches. Ireland, Zimbabwe and Afghanistan are not taking part in this competition, but instead play a program of Test matches with each other and other teams during the same period.

WTC league games are organized by the host nation's cricket board, whereas the final is organized directly by the ICC. The winners of the tournament are awarded the [[ICC Test Championship Mace|Test Mace]], which was previously held by the leader of the [[ICC Men's Test Team Rankings|test team rankings]].

==Popularity==
Supporters of Test cricket, including [[Adam Gilchrist]], argue that it is "the ultimate test of a player's and team's ability".<ref>{{cite web |date=24 June 2009 |title=Adam Gilchrist's Cowdrey Lecture, 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/adam-gilchrist-s-cowdrey-lecture-2009-410365 |access-date=21 December 2008 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |archive-date=26 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226182915/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/adam-gilchrist-s-cowdrey-lecture-2009-410365 |url-status=live}}</ref> However, it has been suggested that Test cricket may be losing popularity, particularly in the face of competition from [[short form cricket]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/sport/cricket/chris-waters-reports-death-test-cricket-have-been-greatly-exaggerated-126971 |title=Chris Waters – Reports of the death of Test cricket have been greatly exaggerated |work=Yorkshire Post |date=9 February 2019 |access-date=27 August 2021 |quote=According to Shashank Manohar, chairman of the International Cricket Council, Test cricket itself "is dying, to be honest". Details of the funeral arrangements will be announced in due course. "Nowadays, people don’t have five days (of) time to watch a Test match", said Manohar. "From ten to five, everybody has their own job to do, so it is very difficult for them to watch this game. T20s get over in three-and-a-half hours, like watching a movie. Therefore, it is picking up very fast." |archive-date=16 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816043258/https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/sport/cricket/chris-waters-reports-death-test-cricket-have-been-greatly-exaggerated-126971 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Day/night cricket|Day/night Test match]]es have been suggested as one way to address this problem.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-cricket-australia-mcgrath/australian-mcgrath-backs-day-night-tests-to-revive-popularity-idUKKCN20K24F |title=Australian McGrath backs day-night tests to revive popularity |last=Ganguly |first=Sudipto |work=Reuters |date=26 February 2020 |access-date=27 August 2021 |archive-date=3 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201203090534/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-cricket-australia-mcgrath/australian-mcgrath-backs-day-night-tests-to-revive-popularity-idUKKCN20K24F |url-status=dead}}</ref> The suggested fall in popularity has been disputed, with a 2019 [[Marylebone Cricket Club]] poll showing that 86% of all cricket fans support Test cricket, more than any other format.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lords.org/lords/news-stories/test-cricket-popularity-strong-as-ever-says-mcc-wo |title=Test Cricket Popularity as Strong as Ever Says MCC World Cricket Committee Following MCC Survey |website=lords.org |date=9 March 2019 |access-date=27 August 2021 |quote=Over 13,000 responders from more than 100 countries took part in the survey, with the majority of responders supporting England, India, Pakistan, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka. Overwhelmingly, Test cricket came out as the format that interests fans the most, regardless of country supported or age. An average of 86% of the responders placed Test cricket as their preferred format to watch, follow and support over One-Day Internationals, T20 Internationals and domestic T20 matches. |archive-date=21 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921105706/https://www.lords.org/lords/news-stories/test-cricket-popularity-strong-as-ever-says-mcc-wo |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2025, after leading Royal Challengers Bangalore to their maiden Indian Premier League title, Virat Kohli stated that “The IPL marks five levels under Test cricket,” highlighting his belief in Test cricket as the superior format in a nation where the sport holds deep cultural importance.<ref>{{cite web |title="I've given everything that I had for the last 18 years to RCB" – Virat Kohli |url=https://www.iplt20.com/video/63927/ive-given-everything-that-i-had-for-the-last-18-years-to-rcb-virat-kohli |website=iplt20.com |access-date=30 June 2025 |archive-date=17 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250917004414/https://www.iplt20.com/video/63927/ive-given-everything-that-i-had-for-the-last-18-years-to-rcb-virat-kohli |url-status=live }}</ref> Furthermore, Test cricket has experienced a revival of interest among fans due to several closely-fought series and the reduction in the number of draws.
